title: Streaming multipart parse shim and guided retry policy for hosted API 5xxs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers reported intermittent 5xx spikes during large multipart/streaming requests. Root cause tracing shows backend deserialization failures when downstream services switched to a new streaming boundary behaviour; many client SDKs retried aggressively which amplified tenant-level traffic and produced cascading 5xxs. This ticket implements a compatibility shim at the request orchestrator to safely parse multipart streaming payloads, adds a replay-safe idempotency reconciliation when parse failures occur, and introduces a guided retry (cooldown + bounded hedging) policy to avoid retry storms.
acceptance_criteria: Multipart streaming payloads that previously caused backend parse errors return 4xx or successful responses instead of 5xx under normal client behaviour
Retry storms are reduced: per-tenant 5xx rate during synthetic burst test drops by >= 80% compared to baseline
No regression in median P95 latency for small requests (<512 tokens) beyond 3%
Canary rollout shows stable error rates across first 10% of tenants for 24h before expanding
Monitoring emits an 'orchestrator.multipart-shim' metric and an alert on shim-exceptions > 0.5% of requests
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the repro harness at https://go/redwood/repro/multipart-streaming (private) to send 1k multipart streaming requests with boundary variations
2) Observe backend decode errors in the streaming parser (logs: streaming/parse#boundary-mismatch) and 5xx spikes in the tenant metrics dashboard
3) Replay the same workload with SDK retries disabled to validate parse success rate differs from default SDK behaviour
4) Run the synthetic client with default SDK retry configuration to confirm amplification and cascade to downstream workers
investigation_notes: Timeline: issue first reported 2026-03-02 by large enterprise customer (ticket INC-1873). Repro harness created 2026-03-05.
Logs: backend streaming parser threw ErrUnexpectedBoundary at ~3.2% of requests for affected tenants. Stacktrace attached in attachments.

Root cause: downstream service upgraded to permissive chunk terminator; our runtime's strict boundary fallback returned a 500 instead of a diagnostic 400 when stream framing didn't match. Client SDKs interpreted 500 as transient and retried immediately.
Amplification: median retry fanout per original request was 4x during incident due to default exponential backoff settings in SDKs and non-idempotent payload markers.
Previous mitigations examined: request-level circuit breakers (existing), tenant quarantine (heavy-handed), and edge normalization (costly).
proposed_solution: 1) Streaming parse shim: tolerant-first parse path in the orchestrator that attempts permissive framing heuristics and emits a diagnostic 400 when the client payload is malformed, falling back to strict parse only after shim fails

2) Replay-safe idempotency reconciliation: when a parse failure is detected, record a short-lived idempotency token and respond with a structured diagnostic that SDKs can interpret as non-retriable (recommendation: error code 'malformed_stream.non_retriable'). Add guidance to SDKs to map this code to no-retry.

3) Guided retry policy: server-side cooldown + bounded hedging for requests that are ambiguous. Implement per-request retry-budget tokens with a short randomized cooldown (50-250ms) to break synchronized retries, and an upper hedging cap of 2 extra attempts within 1s.
4) Observability: new metrics (orchestrator.multipart_shim_attempt, multipart_shim_failures, guided_retry_suppressed), plus a Kibana dashboard for quick triage
5) SDK coordination: doc and PR to SDK repos recommending reaction to 'malformed_stream.non_retriable' and default backoff tuning for streaming endpoints
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy shim to edge-orchestrator in staging, run full repro harness. Duration: 8h
Phase 1 (10% tenants): Enable shim for 10% random hosted tenants with feature-flag 'multipart-shim' for 24h. Monitor errors/latency closely.
Phase 2 (50% tenants): If Phase 1 stable, expand to 50% for 24h and enable idempotency reconciliation. Run targeted customer smoke tests (eng + SE team).
Phase 3 (100%): Full rollout after 72h stable across phases. Post-rollout, keep shim metric alerts sensitivity high for 2 weeks.
Rollback: remove feature flag and revert idempotency token behavior. Pre-approved rollback playbook in attachments.
test_plan: Unit tests for permissive parsing heuristics and exact-match fallback
Integration test using repro harness against canary orchestrator (automated)
Load test: reproduce tenant-burst with default SDK retry settings and validate 5xx reduction target
SDK tests: add mapping for 'malformed_stream.non_retriable' to no-retry in JS and Python SDKs with explicit integration test
Chaos test: simulate downstream slow path to ensure guided retry doesn't increase tail latencies beyond SLOs
monitoring_and_metrics: per-tenant-5xx-rate (existing) - validate drop during synthetic tests
Alert: multipart_shim_failure_rate > 0.5% for 15m triggers P1 on-call workflow
customer_communication: Initial comms: SE outreach sent 2026-03-08 to impacted customers with temporary mitigation (SDK retry disable) and repro steps
Post-fix: prepare a brief technical note to customers explaining improved non-retriable diagnostic, recommended SDK updates, and timeline for full rollout
Support playbook: include steps to toggle feature-flag per-tenant and gather shim logs. Reference: https://confluence.redwood/hosted/multipart-shim-playbook
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer escalation. Repro harness validated boundary mismatch. Assigning to Marco for implementation.

2026-03-11 Marco Chen: Implemented initial permissive parse prototype and local unit tests. Observed shim catches ~92% of repro cases locally. Pushing branch for review: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4567
2026-03-12 Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed prototype, concern about increasing P95 for tiny requests. Suggested randomized cooldown and micro-benchmarks against P95 SLA.

2026-03-13 Marco Chen: Added bounded hedging and randomized cooldown. Load test with 5k rps synthetic tenant shows 78% reduction in retry amplification and minor 1.8% P95 increase for small requests (within target).
2026-03-14 Design review (Liam O'Connor): Accept diagnostic error code format. Recommended explicit SDK deprecation note to avoid long tail of old clients.
2026-03-15 Release manager (Sofia Martinez): Approved canary schedule for 10% tenants starting 2026-03-16. Ensure rollback playbook is staged.
